skill.name: cold-email
skill.description: Drafts concise B2B cold emails, subject lines, CTAs, personalization, and follow-up sequences using proven outreach frameworks.
skill.summary: Creates peer-like B2B cold emails and follow-up sequences with clear CTAs.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

security_audit.summary: Static pattern matches were false positives, including Markdown backticks, ordinary sales language, and anti-pattern examples. The audit found one semantic concern: subject-line guidance may encourage misleading internal-looking outreach. No prompt injection attempt, executable code, network access, or reconnaissance behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace "look internal" guidance with honest, relevant subject lines that clearly match the recipient business context.
Add guidance to follow applicable email laws, honor opt-outs, and avoid contacting people after a breakup email.

semantic_findings.title: Deceptive Subject-Line Framing
semantic_findings.description: The skill advises subject lines that look internal or from a colleague. This can mislead recipients into opening unsolicited outreach.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple references present this framing as an open-rate tactic. The skill includes some trust-preserving guardrails, so the concern is limited.

content.value_statement: Cold outreach often fails because messages feel generic, long, or too pushy. This skill turns prospect context into concise emails, subject lines, CTAs, and follow-ups.
actual_capabilities: Drafts first-touch B2B cold emails with subject lines, opening lines, body copy, and one clear CTA.
Creates three to five email follow-up sequences with fresh angles and respectful breakup emails.
Reviews cold email drafts for clarity, relevance, personalization, tone, and friction.
Applies subject-line, personalization, CTA, and copywriting frameworks from the included references.
Adapts outreach for executives, managers, technical buyers, founders, and sales teams.
Uses benchmark guidance for length, cadence, reply rates, and common mistakes.
limitations: Does not send emails, manage inboxes, or configure automation tools.
Does not verify prospect data, deliverability, consent, or legal compliance.
Needs accurate target audience, product, value, and proof details for strong results.
Focuses on cold B2B outreach, not lifecycle, nurture, or customer marketing campaigns.

use_cases.title: Create SDR Outreach
use_cases.description: Build concise outbound emails for a named persona, problem, proof point, and low-friction reply goal.

use_cases.title: Improve Founder Prospecting
use_cases.description: Turn rough product positioning into short cold emails that test demand with specific buyer segments.

use_cases.title: Review Agency Campaigns
use_cases.description: Audit cold email drafts for weak personalization, feature-heavy copy, poor subject lines, and unclear CTAs.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a First Email
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a first outbound email.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a cold email to [role] at [company type]. We sell [product], solve [problem], and have [proof point].

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for revising existing copy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this cold email for clarity, relevance, subject line, personalization, and CTA. Rewrite it in a stronger peer-like voice: [draft].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Follow-Up Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for a multi-touch campaign.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four-email cold follow-up sequence for [target account]. Rotate angles, add new value each time, and end with a respectful breakup email.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Segmented Campaign
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for multiple buyer groups.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create cold email variants for [segments]. Use different research signals, proof points, subject lines, and CTAs for each seniority level.

output_examples.input: Target VP Marketing at B2B SaaS. Product links content analytics to pipeline. Proof is 3x attributed revenue in 90 days.
output: Noticed many SaaS teams can show traffic, but not which posts create pipeline.
We help marketing teams connect blog performance to revenue. Customers have seen 3x more content-attributed revenue in 90 days.
Worth seeing if the same gap exists on your team?

output_examples.input: Need follow-ups after no reply to an HR software email.
output: Day 3: add a new problem angle and keep the ask simple.
Day 8: share proof from a similar HR team.
Day 14: offer a useful resource or implementation idea.
Day 24: close the loop and honor the final touch.

output_examples.input: Review an email that opens with a generic greeting, a feature list, and a 30-minute meeting request.
output: The draft is sender-focused, vague, and asks for too much too soon.
Rewrite around one relevant problem, one proof point, and a low-friction reply CTA.

best_practices: Provide the target role, company context, proof point, offer, and one relevant research signal.
Ask for multiple subject lines and opening lines when testing a new segment.
Review every message for accuracy, lawful outreach, opt-out handling, and respectful follow-up limits.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for mass spam, scraped lists, or irrelevant outreach.
Do not request fake Re/Fwd lines, false personal claims, or deceptive urgency.
Do not ask for long feature dumps or high-friction meeting requests in the first touch.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates cold email copy, subject lines, personalization angles, CTAs, and follow-up sequences for B2B outreach.

faq.question: Does it send emails for me?
faq.answer: No. It only helps write and review messages. You must use your own email or outreach platform.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing email?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the draft and ask for a review of tone, relevance, subject line, structure, and CTA.

faq.question: What inputs make the output better?
faq.answer: Provide the target buyer, company type, problem, proof point, offer, and any real research signal.

faq.question: Can it write follow-up sequences?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create multi-touch sequences with varied angles, timing guidance, and a final breakup email.

faq.question: Is this for nurture campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It is for cold outbound emails. Lifecycle, nurture, and customer campaigns need different guidance.
